p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting the oxidative reactions of the pentose phosphate pathway. At the top is glucose 6-phosphate. This begins with HCOH in a blue box, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HC. The HCOH in a blue box also bonds up, then right and down to O, which bonds down, then left to HC. HC then bonds down to CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge on it. Below this is an arrow pointing down to 6-phospho-glucano-[gamma]-lactone. To the left of the arrow is glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase. To the right of the arrow is a curved arrow pointing from NADP+ down to NADPH (in a pink box) [plus] H+. In the arc is Mg2+. 6-phospho-glucono-[gamma]-lactone begins with C, which double bonds right to O in a blue box. This bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HC. C in the blue box also bonds up, then right, then down to O, which bonds down, then left to HC. HC then bonds down to CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge on it. Below this is a down arrow pointing to 6-phosphogluconate. To the left of the arrow is lactonase in blue. On the right, H20 bonds to this arrow. Mg2+ is to the right of the arrow. 6-phosphogluconate begins with C, which double bonds up and left to O and bonds up and right to O-. This is all in a blue box. C also bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge on it. Below this is a down arrow pointing to D-ribulose 5-phosphate. To the left of the arrow is 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase in blue. To the right is a curved arrow pointing from NADP+ down to NADPH (in a red box) [plus] H+. In the arc is Mg2+. There is also an arrow jutting right to CO2 in blue. D-ribulose 5-phosphate begins with C, which bonds up to CH2OH, double bonds right to O, and bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge on it. Below this are reversible arrows. To the left of the arrows is phosphopentose isomerase in blue. Below this is D-ribose 5-phosphate in a pink box, where CHO bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to HCOH, which bonds down to CH2OPO3 with a minus 2 charge on it.
